Apologies if this is the wrong subvoat. I'll be flying into Guangzhou and staying around Shunde for a week. I speak no Mandarin. What are some do's and don'ts I should follow? Also, what are some things I should try and go see? Thanks!

Edit: Thanks everyone for the input!
Visiting for business. What are some do's and don'ts?

I speak no Mandarin.

Oh you are going to have a fun time, for sure...

Just make sure you do not mention the thing that did not happen in the square.

I'm not familiar with that area, so can't give specific siteseeing tips.

Since you said business trip, I assume you will be having at least one meal with some local business people. If you are not a heavy drinker, then make a good excuse for not drinking (e.g. medical) early on. The baijiu often catches people out. If you are planning to drink, then this is done either when someone toasts you, or you toasting someone else. No taking sips by yourself. Let the host direct you to your seat rather than choosing it yourself.

If you go out wandering by yourself, watch out for scams. Safety will be good, unless you go out of your way to an unsavoury location. Standard scam around tourism areas is someone wanting to practice English, suggesting some place to go for tea/meal/drink, and then trying to overcharge you for it.

Don't expect taxi drivers, tourism staff (ticket sellers), or serving staff to be able to speak English (although some might). Take a hotel card with the name and address of the hotel in Chinese on it with you when you head out. It is possible to get around and do quite a bit without speaking any Chinese if you are comfortable in doing so. My first visit I spoke no Chinese at all apart from badly pronouncing hello and thankyou and managed to get around.

  • learn how to say knee how and shay shay
  • learn how to say nei hou and do ze (because lol GZ)
  • don't go to KTV alone
  • use common sense
  • if you get in to trouble, you are foreign and therefore the bad guy.

Be careful with phones, tablets and laptops. They tend to get infected (and scanned) while in China. You may consider leaving them at home, and buy supercheap disposable one's to use while in China. If you get stuck drinking Baijiu, know that it is usually 104 proof (sometimes higher, sometimes lower). 1. Install QQ International on your laptop (mobile is in chinese so may not help) and then get WeChat on your phone.

Within 24 hours after joining English Practice Chat Groups you will be able to find people in Guangzhou who may be delighted to act as Guides/Translators and often in exchange for the english practice and you paying for meals.

If you want to be more professional (and you may want that) hiring a translator - often an english major from a local Uni - that can be a massive help that actually pays for itself in saved bad choices/mistranslations AND really helps you use time as best as possible. Interesting side benefit: You might be far less likely to get gamed and charged Laowai price. I often hire a translator from the local Uni if I have some complicated visa paperwork or hospital visits. Its so damn worth the 15rmb an hour and lunch the efficiency she brings and she monitors taxi drivers who may try and take the extra-long route.

Guangzhou is actually pretty decent for International business and tourism so you aren't really going to be that bad off without Mandarin or being a first-timer foreigner. You have a good chance of running into other foreigners (if you see African dudes they often speak english too) and I'm always amazed how many Guangzhou people actually know a good little bit of English.

Canton Tower is a bit expensive for the crazy bubble car ride thing at the top and maybe supertouristy but I think its pretty awesome. Speaking of touristy but Guangzhou Zoo and come on.. Pandas!

Not sure what your whole schedule might allow but sometimes people forget but Guangzhou and Shenzhen and Foshan and Donguan and Huizhou are practically one 'super city'.

What that means is that if you're googling about or looking for things for sure expand to those areas IF there is something awesome because you can get there by express coach / subway combo / taxi combo and in less than 2 hours.

Shunde itself .. I can't actually think of any one outstanding thing other than the buffets were pretty damn great IMO and you'll see them on the streets (grab a tray and point at what you want heh) and it seemed to me there was quite a lot of KTV/adult oriented entertainment clubs.

If you are doing business with Chinese you should prepare for 3-6 hour long dinners where they sit around tables and bring out many dishes and holy efffff can they drink. Chinese wine is somehow 220% alcohol so be forewarned. And they will happily get you fall-down drunk if you let them.

Honestly I find Guangzhou kinda annoying. For whatever reason its difficult to walk around, find things, strangely pushy yet slow yet poorly organized for city buses yet I cant explain it but we always find it annoying to get around Guangzhou. Taxi drivers were actually pretty good and honest in our cases though.

when i first heard about free jazz the idea really appealed to me, however i found most of the selections i listened to very challenging- specifically free jazz by ornette coleman. i just didn't have the right foundation to really understand it but thankfully i had a friend who gently directed me to the shallow end of jazz pool explaining that the deep end would still be around when i was ready for it. although with a bit more experience under my belt i have come to appreciate that fantastic album i still find i like a little more structure than free jazz offers.

after a few years of working my way through the great standards of jazz i was introduced to the world saxaphone quartet. i really liked how their approach to what i consider fusion involved jazz and african music rather than the more common jazz/rock or jazz/funk blends. i had recently discovered fela kuti, franco luambo & ok jazz, and king sunny ade so the mix of the world saxaphone quartet's influences was very timely and really appealing to me.

when i started to explore the various members of the world saxaphone quartet's solo work my interest with julius hemphill lead me to a copy of dogon a.d. in an used record store. when i first heard it i knew i had found the right balance between improvesation and structure for me and it remains one of my favorite albums.
